## 21 Nov 2026 — Crawl freshness: sitemap `lastmod` = when the page really last changed, site-wide (body dates per family, articles dated by their last reader-visible publish, 29N phases); sitemap resubmission script (deploy only; no publish group; no title, description or lead touched)

**Why.** Google is not re-reading pages after we change them. Search Console last-crawl dates on 20 Nov: `/es/rodalies/r1/`
and `/r4/` 30 Oct, `/ca/rodalies/` 29 Oct, `/es/embalses/` 1 Nov, `/es/gasolineras/` 6 Nov,
`/es/guias/semana-santa-2027-cataluna/` 16 Nov, `/es/avisos/` unknown. We ship body changes daily to thousands of pages, and
the sitemap told Google most of them had not changed since 28–30 Oct.

**Findings (measured 20–21 Nov).**

1. *Sitemap `lastmod` sources* (live sitemap of 21 Nov, release c8b6ae3, 2,888 URLs, 1.55 MB: one file is far inside the
   50,000-URL / 50 MB limits; robots.txt lists `/sitemap.xml` and `/news-sitemap.xml`; every one of the 2,888 URLs answers 200
   at the origin, none is noindex, every canonical is the URL itself):

   | Family (URLs) | `lastmod` came from | Live 21 Nov | Wrong because |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | Elections ca/es/en (924) | results snapshot read day (`latestDataDate`) | 30 Oct, all 924 | polling places 2 Nov, mesa 4 Nov, polling section 16–19 Nov, 29N layer 18 Nov, model 20 Nov never showed; `/es/elecciones/barcelona/` last crawled **28 Oct** |
   | Holiday towns/hubs/dates (797) | `NEXT_YEAR.readOn ?? SNAPSHOT.readOn` | 30 Oct (794) | 2027 local days for 302 + 72 more towns (4, 17, 20 Nov), next-holiday line, .ics block, CTR titles: frozen read day |
   | Spain 2027 (421) | `SOURCES_READ_ON` / latest reading | 20 Nov (386), day pages 6 Nov (29) | day pages changed 18–20 Nov |
   | Calculators (120) | each `RULES_AS_OF` / snapshot | 13 Nov (54), down to 28 May (average salary) | WebApplication schema 19 Nov, kinship table, "más calculadoras" links: rule dates only |
   | Christmas fairs (95) | each town's check day | 13 Nov (90) | 33-town re-read and copy 20 Nov |
   | Weekend (26), gordo, lottery checkers, polls | snapshot read / page constant | 11–19 Nov | template changes after |
   | Rodalies, fuel, PVPC, butane, warnings, today | read at render (34b7e03, live since 20 Nov 18:55) | today / this hour | right (kept) |
   | Reservoirs (30) | ACA latest reading | 20 Nov | right (kept) |
   | Database articles: guides, strikes, legal (≈380 of the 401 non-programmatic URLs) | `entry_translations.updated_at` = dateModified, moved only when the facts are re-verified (article-dates.ts rule 3) | Easter 2027 guide **31 Oct** | body-only changes never moved it: Easter 2027 was republished with new content on 4, 11, 17, 18 and 20 Nov and stayed at 31 Oct (last crawl 16 Nov) |
   | Home, hubs, author pages | newest article `updated_at` | 20 Nov | right source, inherited the article gap |

2. *Google is not reading the sitemap.* Search Console sitemaps report (API, 21 Nov): `/sitemap.xml` submitted 17 Nov 12:41,
   **last read 17 Nov 12:41** (only when submitted), 3,413 URLs submitted (the pre-cleanup count; live has 2,888);
   `/news-sitemap.xml` read daily (last 21 Nov 04:56), 9 URLs, 0 errors. The origin log agrees: in 3.5 days Googlebot fetched
   robots.txt 386 times and `/sitemap.xml` **0** times (the sitemap is `max-age=0, must-revalidate`, Cloudflare `EXPIRED`,
   so every fetch would reach the origin). The news sitemap holds the last 48 h of news-type pages (9 = 3 pieces × 3 locales).
3. *Crawl health* (Caddy log, Googlebot verified against Google's published IP ranges; 24 spoofed "Googlebot" requests
   excluded; the log only keeps 18 Nov 02:09 → 21 Nov 11:47 because it rolls at 50 MiB × 10 files, so no 14-day view; with
   Cloudflare in front the origin sees only cache misses and bypassed requests, so these are lower bounds and Search Console
   Crawl stats is the full picture): **1,043 / 1,104 / 1,162 requests a day** (18/19/20 Nov; 848 by 11:47 on 21 Nov).
   By family over the window: elections 1,296 (842 URLs), holidays 1,266 (836), robots/sitemaps 388, static 367, guides 344
   (108), Spain 2027 201 (137), live pages 142 (104), home 51, fairs 15, calculators 8. Status: 4,022 × 200, 23 × 304,
   32 × 307/308, 80 × 404 (75 old `/_next/static` chunks after deploys, 5 legacy WordPress URLs), **0 × 5xx, no timeouts**
   (3 requests over 5 s). Response time p50 109 ms, p95 621 ms, p99 1.6 s (live pages p95 2.0 s). **52 % of Googlebot's HTML
   hits (1,758 of 3,350) go to URLs not in the sitemap**: the noindex low-demand town pages (`/ca/festius/` 495,
   `/ca/eleccions/` 417, `/es/festivos/` 304, `/es/elecciones/` 214), past 11N city strike pages 145, fuel place pages 75 —
   expected while Google confirms the noindex, and the reason calculators get 8 hits in 3.5 days.
4. *Freshness signals on pages.* HTML carries an ETag (weak through Caddy's gzip) and no `Last-Modified`; `If-None-Match`
   gets 304 at the edge and `If-Modified-Since` gets 200, so a changed page can never be answered "not modified".
   Cache-Control: static families `s-maxage=31536000` (purged by every deploy and publish), guides `s-maxage=86400, swr`, live
   pages 300–1800 s, home 3600 s; Cloudflare HIT on cached pages, MISS after the 00:05 deploy purge. The sitemap's
   `Last-Modified` is the response time (added at the edge; harmless, Google reads `lastmod`). JSON-LD `dateModified` and the
   visible "updated" date follow the verification rules on purpose (lib/seo/article-dates.ts: Google News forbids freshening
   without new information), elections/holidays carry their dataset's read day: both unchanged.
5. *Discovery.* The new pages are linked from crawled hubs: `/es/avisos/` and `/en/fuel-prices-catalonia/` from the home
   footer (home crawled 21 Nov), strike day pages from `/es/` and `/es/guias/`, the 46 new Spain 2027 city pages from their
   community hub. URL inspection 21 Nov (22 URLs, `docs/growth/baseline/crawl-freshness-2026-11-21.json`): 21 indexed,
   `/en/fuel-prices-catalonia/` unknown; last crawl `/es/rodalies/r1/` and `/r4/` 30 Oct, `/es/elecciones/barcelona/`
   28 Oct, Spain 2027 city pages 13–15 Nov, `/es/guias/semana-santa-2027-cataluna/` 16 Nov, `/es/festivos/2027/` 14 Nov,
   `/es/calculadoras/sueldo-neto/` and `salario-minimo-2027/` 14 Nov, `/es/mercados-navidad/` 17 Nov; already recrawled
   after the 20 Nov live-data fix: `/ca/rodalies/` 21 Nov, `/es/gasolineras/`, `/es/embalses/`, `/es/avisos/` 20 Nov.
   IndexNow (`scripts/indexnow-sitemap.py`, the publish route) reaches Bing, Yandex and Seznam only; Google ignores it and
   retired the sitemap ping in 2023. What Google honours is an accurate `lastmod` it reads, and a sitemap it re-reads.

**What changed.**

- `src/lib/seo/body-dates.ts` + `body-dates.json`: every code-rendered family (55 `dated("<key>", …)` wraps in
  `src/app/sitemap.ts`) is dated no earlier than its **body date**, the moment the code and data files that render its pages
  last changed. `scripts/body-dates.ts` finds those files (the family's route files from its own sitemap URLs, their imports
  inside the content folders, minus the site chrome and minus other families reached only through cross-links) and
  fingerprints them on normalised source (comments and formatting move nothing; a string, number, link or data row does).
  At deploy, `prebuild` re-dates a family whose fingerprint differs from the live release's **to the build time**, the
  moment the change goes live; the others keep the live release's date (`BODY_DATES_PREVIOUS` from deploy.sh, or
  `../../current` itself; it can never fail the build). Locally, `npm run seo:body-dates` dates a changed family by its last
  real commit; `--check`, `--explain <key>`.
- Database articles: `lastmod` = latest of dateModified, `entries.updated_at` (now written by publish-article.ts **only** when
  an edition is new or its title, lead, SEO fields or body changed, or the hero image, category or source list changed; the
  institutional-pages publisher no longer stamps it), today for day-dependent blocks (unchanged), and the body date of any
  code-data block the article carries (local holidays table, Christmas shops, tourist tax, transport passes, municipal
  elections, election history). Hubs and author pages take the newest article `lastmod`.
- Elections: never older than the 29N phase the pages print (`electionPhaseStart`: 28 Nov 00:00, 29 Nov 00:00 and 20:00,
  30 Nov, 8 Dec; the sitemap revalidates hourly).
- `scripts/gsc-sitemaps.py`: `list` (the report above) and `submit --yes` (Search Console `sitemaps.submit` for both
  sitemaps). Not run.
- Effect on the live sitemap's code-rendered URLs (2,484): 2,428 move forward, e.g. elections 30 Oct → 20 Nov (924),
  holiday towns 30 Oct → 20 Nov (794), Spain 2027 day pages 6 Nov → 20 Nov, calculators 13 Nov → 18–19 Nov, fairs 13 Nov →

**Not changed, on purpose.** Titles, descriptions, H1s and leads (windows above). JSON-LD `dateModified` and visible dates
(article-dates.ts rules). The single sitemap file (inside the limits; a split by family would only add per-family indexed
counts in Search Console). Noindex decisions and the low-demand list. Caddy log retention (`roll_keep 10` keeps ~3.5 days;
raising it to 40 would give the 14-day view: owner decision, disk). Granularity: the holiday town, comarca and date pages share
one route (`[municipi]`), so a date-page change re-dates the towns too.

**Prediction.** Within 14 days of the deploy plus resubmission: Search Console shows `/sitemap.xml` read after the
resubmission and again without one; Googlebot origin requests reach `/sitemap.xml` at least weekly; at least 15 of the 22
URLs show a last crawl after the deploy (elections Barcelona, Rodalies R1/R4, Spain 2027 cities, Easter 2027, calculators);
`/en/fuel-prices-catalonia/` indexed. Crawl requests per day (Search Console Crawl stats) up ≥ 20 % on the 14 days before.
Wrong if on 5 Dec the sitemap's last read is still the resubmission day, or fewer than 8 of the 22 URLs were crawled after it.

**Confounders.** The 20 Nov live-data entry (same Rodalies/fuel/reservoir URLs; already recrawling). 29N (election pages
get demand and links: crawl rises anyway — compare the elections share with the other families). The core update rolling out
(18 Nov entry). Owner "Request indexing" clicks on single URLs (note which).

Every page: one 15.7 KB (br) stylesheet flagged render-blocking (100–450 ms estimated), 170–190 KB of JS (React DOM and the
Next router are 46–50 KB of "unused" JS), 108 KB of preloaded fonts (Plex variable 41 KB + Fraunces 67.5 KB), no
third-party request (GA only after consent; **no AdSense script is loaded anywhere**: 0 `adsbygoogle`, 0 `<ins>`, only the
`google-adsense-account` meta). Rodalies was not run (same live template as the fuel hub; call budget).

**Server side.** curl from the VPS through Cloudflare: HTML HIT 0.09–0.26 s, MISS 0.37–1.9 s (paga extra 1.9 s, strike
0.82 s, Canyelles 0.77 s, Montserrat 0.62 s). Caddy origin log 21 Nov 01:11–12:34 UTC (19,676 origin requests): HTML for
people p50 31 ms, p75 78 ms, p90 198 ms, p99 1.16 s; `/_next/image` (bypassed at Cloudflare) p50 122 ms, p90 453 ms.

**Top three, with evidence.**
1. **TTFB/cache misses** are the largest share of field LCP (TTFB p75 0.6 s of 1.7 s; 4 % poor > 1.8 s). A Cloudflare MISS
   costs 0.4–1.9 s against 0.1–0.25 s for a HIT. Not code.
2. **Image-hero templates** (guides, strike days, day trips; `/es/guias/` is a third of impressions) are the only ones with lab
   LCP over 2 s. In the waterfall the hero (fetchpriority high, preloaded) shares the first window with the two fonts, the
   stylesheet and the header mark, all "High"; the mark (36 px) only because React's server renderer preloads every
   non-lazy `<img>` that is not `fetchPriority="low"`. Real phones also fetch big heroes: origin log, mobile user agents,
   w=1200 54 KB, w=1600 90 KB on average.
3. **Consent card on election town pages** (not changed, owner rule): Playwright lab (412×823 @1.75, 1.6 Mbps/150 ms, CPU ×2,
   3 runs each) `/es/elecciones/barcelona/` first visit LCP 4.18 s (3.92–4.64), card paragraph = LCP element 3/3, vs
   2.43 s (2.37–2.74) with the cookie answered: **+1.75 s**. On `/es/festivos/barcelona/` the card is no longer the LCP
   element (the 19 Nov answer-first lead is bigger): 3.57 s (2.66–4.31) vs 3.47 s (2.45–3.59), noise. In PSI the election
   H1 (27,500 px²) and the card paragraph are about the same size, so the LCP element flips with fonts and viewport. Field
   LCP still passes at the origin; the cost lands on first visits only, i.e. ~90 % of visitors.

**Changes.**
- `src/components/Wordmark.tsx`: the mark gets `fetchPriority="low"` (still `loading="eager"`). React then emits no
  `<link rel="preload" as="image">` for it, so the hero (articles) or the fonts and stylesheet (everything else) are the only
  high-priority requests in the first window, and every page drops one origin request from it.
- `src/components/pages/EntryArticle.tsx` + `src/lib/layout/hero-image.ts`: hero `sizes` =
  `(max-width: 47.99rem) and (min-resolution: 2.5dppx) 70vw, 100vw`. What-if on production (HTML rewritten, Chromium):
  412 px @2.625 1080w → 828w, 393/430 px @3 1200w → 828w, 412 px @3.5 1600w → 1080w; strike guide hero 33–62 KB → 21–33 KB,
  Montserrat 51–128 KB → 32–51 KB; effective density 1.9–2.6x; 1.75 and 2 dppx phones, tablets and desktops unchanged; a
  browser without `resolution` in `sizes` reads 100vw. The head preload carries the same string (one request).
- Test: `tests/lcp-image-priority.test.ts`.

**Expected effect.** Field: LCP on the image-hero templates a little earlier on ≥ 2.5 dppx phones (20–75 KB less on the LCP
request; the slow tail gains most: the bridge guide has 7 % of loads over 2.5 s). No pass/fail change: everything already
passes. Lab: the PSI phone is 1.75 dppx, so its hero is unchanged; only the mark leaves the head preloads.

**Not changed, and why.**
- Consent card: owner rule (numbers above). AdSense: not loaded, nothing to measure.
- `experimental.inlineCss` (would remove the render-blocking stylesheet, ~1 RTT for new visitors): experimental, duplicates
  the CSS in the RSC payload (+15–30 KB br on every HTML, ISR cache and crawls), cannot be checked without a build. Candidate
  for its own measured trial.
- Fonts: dropping the Fraunces preload or its `opsz` axis would free ~67 KB of the first window on hero pages, at the cost of
  heading swap shifts on Android (no metric-matched local fallback there) or the brand cut. Field CLS is 100 % good; left.
- Framework JS (React DOM, router) and the 11 KB block-renderer chunk on articles: not worth a refactor at TBT 4–47 ms.
- Owner, free, outside the code: (a) Cloudflare **Tiered Cache → Smart Tiered Caching** to raise the HTML hit ratio (point
  1). (b) `/api/fuel/catalonia/` is bypassed at Cloudflare (rule 3, `/api/`) while upstream.ts assumes an hour of CDN cache:
  every call re-reads the Ministry list (origin p50 1.66 s, p90 3.5 s; PSI: the fetch took 3.3 s and the re-rank landed at
  4.3 s, main thread 821 ms, the highest of the ten). Fix = a cache rule for that path or a 5-minute in-process memo like
  `fuel/server.ts`; not done here (live-data behaviour, 10 calls in 11 h). (c) Meta's link-preview bot `HatchFeed`
  (agent.meta.ai) took 2,680 of 3,886 `/_next/image` responses and 343 of 398 MB in those 11 h (1600/1920 w), over the same
  origin link the readers use.

**Re-test after deploy.**
1. `curl -s https://www.catalunyainfo.com/es/guias/huelga-26-noviembre/ | grep -o 'imageSizes="[^"]*"'` → the new string;
   `grep -c 'rel="preload" as="image" imageSrcSet="/_next/image/?url=%2Ficon-192'` → 0 (no head preload for the mark).
2. Rerun the what-if script unmodified (`whatif-hero-sizes.js` in the scratchpad tools): 393 px @3 must fetch 828w, once.
3. pagespeed.web.dev on the 10 URLs (links in the scratchpad `*.field.json`): the mark's request "Low", hero alone "High".

spain" 3.9k, "nie spain" 4.1k, "beckham law" 1.2k a month; row 7: "tramos irpf" ≈ 12k. The site had the NIE/TIE and padró
guides (13 Nov) and a Beckham mode inside the net salary calculator (18 Nov), but no page with the IRPF scales and no
page answering "beckham law requirements / how to apply / deadline". Results read on 21 Nov disagree on the Catalan scale
(six, eight or nine bands; first rate 9.5, 10.5 or 12 %); the law has eight bands from 9.5 %.

**What changed.**
1. *New: income tax brackets 2026* (`src/lib/content/batch02/income-tax.ts`, key `incomeTax`):
   `/ca/guies/trams-irpf-catalunya/`, `/es/guias/tramos-irpf-cataluna/`, `/en/guides/income-tax-spain-catalonia/`.
   State scale (LIRPF art. 63.1, unchanged since 2021: 9.5–24.5 %), Catalan scale (art. 611-1 Codi tributari, rewritten by
   Decret llei 5/2025 from 1 Jan 2025: 8 bands, 9.5–25.5 %; ATC lists no 2026 scale change), combined marginal table (19 %
   to 50 % above 300,000 €, computed), savings scale (BOE 19–30 %), residence (art. 9, 183 days), worldwide income (art. 2,
   art. 80 relief), non-residents (TRLIRNR 24 / 19 %), worked examples 25k–150k gross from the calculator engine (SS,
   base, withholding) with both scales and the 5,550 € minimum (Catalonia keeps it: AEAT manual, art. 611-2), the Renta
   difference, who files (art. 96: 22,000 / 15,876 €), Renta 2025 opened 8 Apr 2026, Renta WEB Open, Catalan deduction
   names (no amounts), mistakes, 8-question FAQ. No photo (noPhotoReason).
2. *New: the Beckham law* (`src/lib/content/batch02/beckham-law.ts`, key `beckhamLaw`): `/ca/guies/llei-beckham-regim-impatriats/`,
   `/es/guias/ley-beckham-regimen-impatriados/`, `/en/guides/beckham-law-spain/`. Every rule from
   `net-salary/special-regime.ts`, re-read 21 Nov (LIRPF art. 93; RIRPF 115–119; AEAT regime, G606, 151 instructions,
   non-residents manual): conditions table (art. 93.1), what you pay (24 / 47 %, gross base, all pay deemed Spanish, other
   foreign income untaxed, one scale 50/50, wealth tax obligación real, no treaty residence), comparison against the
   income-tax guide's scales (crossover 55,040 € for a single person in Catalonia; −1,664 € at 40k, +8,348 € at 100k),
   six steps to opt in, eight deadlines, family (93.3), waiver and exclusion (no return), what it does not change,
   mistakes, 9-question FAQ in the query wording. No photo.

dataset `data.renfe.com/dataset/horarios-cercanias`), read 21 Nov 2026: CKAN `license_id` **CC-BY-4.0**, resource
`last_modified` 2026-11-21T03:09:19. data.renfe.com/legal (read 21 Nov): cite "Origen de los datos: Renfe Operadora", give
the last-update date, do not distort, do not suggest Renfe takes part in or sponsors the reuse. Each summary prints all
three (ca/es/en) and the source is listed with the others. The build refuses another licence id. The feed is one file for
all Spanish Cercanías networks, one service per day, ~30 days ahead: 21 Nov–20 Dec 2026, **no Rodalies trips 30 Nov–4 Dec**
(printed on the pages). Replacement buses are route type 3 under the line's name (R3 Barcelona–Centelles/Vic, R13 La
Plana–Lleida now): counted apart, never as trains. The download was saved in a fresh directory outside the repo and parsed
by the repo script as bytes (CRC-checked zip reader `scripts/lib/zip.ts`); only the derived snapshot is committed.

**What changed.**

   (`npm run rodalies-timetable:snapshot -- build | check`), `timetable.json` (the snapshot, 158 KB). Per line and

reuse a download), review the diff, `node --test … tests/rodalies-timetable.test.ts`, commit, deploy. **Every 14 days**
(next by 5 Dec 2026) and at once after a timetable change Renfe or Rodalies announce, or a works closure starts or ends.
The test fails 21 days after the build (12 Dec 2026) or after the feed's last day (20 Dec 2026), whichever is first; the
pages hide the summary themselves after the feed's last day. `-- check` says whether data.renfe.com has a newer file.

## 22 Nov 2026 — New family: ZBE (low-emission zones) by city — Barcelona, Tarragona, Girona, Reus + a hub with the DGT's list for the rest of Spain, "can I drive in with my label?" and "does it apply today?", ca + es + en (deploy, then group `zbe`) (review 2026-12-06 and 2026-12-20)

**Why.** Second of the two evergreen families chosen on 22 Nov (the first, zona azul by city, is the entry above): a concrete
answer + place + date, asked every day of the year, where the results are council PDFs, old news and pages without the
rule of the day.

**What ships (15 URLs).**

- Hub: `/es/zbe/`, `/ca/zbe/`, `/en/low-emission-zones/`. The four Catalan cities with their rule, the Catalan zones not yet
  written, and the rest of the DGT's zones as a list (name, municipality, link to the council) **without access rules**:
  a rule is printed only for a city whose council pages have been read.
- One page per city in the three languages, same slug: `barcelona`, `tarragona`, `girona`, `reus`. First screen: the answer
  by DGT label (0, ECO, C, B, none) as a table — "yes" only where the council names the label, "no" with its days and
  hours and who is still let in, "it depends" with the council's condition (Reus: label B in NO2 episodes; no label by
  where the vehicle pays its tax) — and, computed in the browser with the clock of Spain and the city's public holidays,
  whether the restriction applies today and at this hour. Then days and hours, map and streets, since when and announced
  changes, exemptions and permits (residents, occasional days, car parks, foreign plates), cameras and fine, what the DGT
  file says and where it differs from the council, **what the page does not publish** (the official pages are silent),
  FAQ in the searched words, official sources.
- Titles: "ZBE Tarragona: etiquetas, horario, mapa y multa" / "ZBE Girona: etiquetes, horari, mapa i multa" / "Reus
  low-emission zone (ZBE): labels, hours, fines". All ≤ 60; descriptions ≤ 155 (held by `tests/zbe.test.ts`).

**Sources and method.** Every restriction and fact in `src/lib/programmatic/zbe/cities.ts` carries the index of its
source and the council's own sentence, verbatim. Barcelona: zbe.barcelona (AMB) and the AMB register pages. Tarragona:
tarragona.cat (FAQ, calendar, map). Girona: web.girona.cat/zbe (characteristics, calendar, exemptions, control, FAQ).
Reus: mobilitat.reus.cat/zbe (zone, calendar, FAQ). Fine where the council gives no amount: the traffic act
(BOE-A-2015-11722, arts. 76 z3, 80.1 and 94). Hub list: the DGT's DATEX II files at the National Access Point
(`nap.dgt.es`, CC BY 4.0), committed as a snapshot of 22 Nov 2026 (59 zones).

Re-check by hand on 22 Nov, 23:00 (after the agent that built the branch stopped): all 16 source URLs answered 200 and
each of the 40 quoted sentences was found on its live page (three only after ignoring the spaces the pages' inline tags
leave: "laborables .", "A qui afecta :", "NO 2"). The figures the text adds around the quotes were read too (24 daily
authorisations and the yearly fee, 15 days for the foreign-plate check, 12 and 24 occasional days, the 30 % for repeat
offences, 100 euros for prompt payment in Girona). One correction came out of it: Reus's FAQ 1.6 does say how the zone
is enforced (cameras that read plates against the DGT list and the council register); the page said "not published" and
now quotes it.

## 2026-11-23 — 29N town pages: origin cost per page view (election links prefetch on intent; deploy warms the election routes before the purge; no title, description, H1, lead or visible content touched; deploy only, no publish group)

**Why.** Before 29N (goal 30k sessions that day) the election town pages (`/ca/eleccions/<town>/`, `/es/elecciones/…`,
`/en/elections/…`, 947 + 947 + 30, `revalidate = 300`) were slow on a cold cache. Owner's live measurements, 23 Nov, right
after the 19:19 deploy and its full Cloudflare purge: Súria 3.7 s (es) / 2.7 s (ca), Sabadell 1.8 s, Barcelona 1.4 s,
Girona 1.2 s; Cloudflare HITs 0.5–0.7 s; during a ~2 req/s crawl several took 8–11 s and 290 URLs took > 3 s.

**Where the time goes** (measured 23 Nov 2026 on the VPS; a copy of the live standalone build, release
20261123T175956Z-e851218, run on port 3199 without the database, profiled with the V8 inspector; plus ≤ 1 req/s probes of
production through Cloudflare and on 127.0.0.1:3000):
- **Not the database, not fetches, not data loading.** The page reads the committed snapshot (no query, no fetch); the
  header/footer counts are memoised in-process for 10 min. `generateMetadata` costs 1–2 ms; `resolveElectionPage` is a
  `Set` check plus a `find` over 947 towns. The 1.8 MB results snapshot and the 1.6 MB polling-place JSON are parsed once per
  process, not per render.
- **Cold process after a restart: 7–9 s** for the first town page (the route loads ≥ 5.3 MB of server chunks, among them the
  two snapshots, and runs cold code), 0.5–3 s for the next few, ~0.2 s once warm. A deploy restarts the process and then
  purges Cloudflare, so the first visitors of every route land on that cold start at once — the owner's 3.7 s Súria.
- **A warm cold-render costs ~0.2–0.25 s of CPU** on the one Node thread (40 towns sequential: mean 0.27 s, p50 0.21 s,
  p90 0.50 s; production direct on 127.0.0.1:3000: 0.09–0.35 s). Split: React render + Flight serialisation ~35 %, the ISR
  write ~20 % (Next's `IncrementalCache.set` runs `JSON.stringify` over the whole entry, buffers included, then writes
  `.html`, `.rsc`, `.meta` and four `.segments` files: ~0.5–0.8 MB per town, 0.8 MB for Barcelona), GC ~8 %, the ETag hash
  of the HTML ~5 %, the app's own code (model, page component) ~10 % (~20 ms). It scales with the page (HTML 180–320 KB,
  RSC 100–160 KB), which is content: not changed.
- **One thread saturates at ~4–5 renders/s.** 24 cold towns at concurrency 8 took 9.3 s wall (0.39 s each). A STALE hit is
  not free either: Next resolves the stale entry and starts the regeneration in the same tick
  (`next/dist/server/response-cache/index.js`, `handleGet`), so on one thread its latency is close to a render's (local:
  STALE p50 0.22 s vs MISS 0.21 s). A cache HIT is ~25 ms of CPU.
- **Viewport prefetches multiply the origin work per page view.** Cloudflare caches the HTML but never `?_rsc=`. In headless
  Chromium on the build copy (390 px phone, scrolled to the end): a town page sent **12** RSC requests (route tree +
  segment, ~10–20 ms each at the origin, a full render when the target is stale or never rendered: comarca 0.1–0.4 s), from
  the election-night guide (3: linked from the next-step box and the related list), the comarca link (2), the hub link (2)
  and the five other guide links (5); a comarca page sent **6 and
  more** (its 42 other-comarca links drip through the prefetch scheduler). 18 Nov Caddy logs had RSC prefetches at 41 % of
  origin requests; header, footer, breadcrumbs, hub lists and sibling lists were already fixed then, these were not.
- Network: TCP retransmits 4.3 % of segments since boot (3.83 M / 88.2 M, 644 k RTO timeouts; 0.6 % over 30 s tonight).
  Multi-second outliers through Cloudflare can be retransmission timeouts, not render time.

**What changed.**
1. **Election links prefetch on intent** (`IntentLink`, the 18 Nov pattern): town page `ElectionResultsPage.tsx` comarca,
   hub and guide links; comarca page `ElectionsComarcaPage.tsx` other comarques, hub, guides; and the sitewide next-step
   box `NextStep.tsx` (near the top of every page that has it). Same `<a href>` HTML (checked against the live build's HTML
   for Súria); a hover, focus or touch still prefetches, so the click stays a client-side navigation. Town lists keep
   `prefetch={false}`. Test: `tests/election-prefetch.test.ts`.
2. **`ops/vps/deploy.sh` warms the election routes** after the health checks and before the Cloudflare purge (one town page
   per language, two comarca pages, the three hubs; `--max-time 60`, never fails the deploy; ~5–10 s). Test:
   `tests/cdn-purge.test.ts`. Takes effect for deploys only after `sudo bash /srv/catalunyainfo/current/ops/vps/provision.sh
   --files-only` installs the new `/usr/local/bin/catalunyainfo-deploy`.

**Expected gain.** Per scrolled town page view: 12 uncached origin requests → 0 (1–2 when the reader hovers or taps a link),
i.e. ~0.15–0.25 s of origin CPU per view removed, plus the comarca/hub renders those prefetches triggered; per comarca page
view: 6–40+ → 0. The town page itself, cached by Cloudflare, costs the origin one render per Cloudflare POP per 5 min, so on
the night most of the per-view origin work was the prefetches. After a deploy: the first visitors no longer pay the 7–9 s
cold start. Per-render cost is unchanged (~0.2–0.25 s CPU).

**Not changed, and why.**
- *Prerendering more towns at build time:* the build takes ~15 min (893 s; static generation 276 s), so entries prerendered
  with `revalidate = 300` are already stale at go-live and a STALE hit costs about a render on one thread. Little gain for
  +~1 min of build and ~0.3 GB per release.
- *A longer revalidate before 20:00 and a short one after:* the town pages print no figures on the night (results reach them
  only through `npm run elections:29n -- import` → `snapshot.ts` → deploy, after the 4–7 Dec general count;
  `scripts/elections-29n.ts`, `tests/election-29n-import.test.ts`), so the 300 s exists for the clock-driven phase (28 Nov
  00:00, 29 Nov 00:00, 29 Nov 20:00, 30 Nov 00:00, 8 Dec 00:00) and the day-dependent boxes. Next 16 without
  `cacheComponents` needs `revalidate` as a literal, and no timer revalidates at the boundaries, so a timed switch is not
  clean. Recommendation: keep 300 through 29 Nov; a deploy on Mon 30 Nov can raise it to 900 (the "after" phase changes only
  at midnight); back to `false` after 8 Dec as planned.
- *`generateEtags: false`:* ~5 % of a render, ~10 % of a HIT, but it changes 304 behaviour sitewide. Left as it is.

**Recommendations (owner/ops).** Turn on Cloudflare Smart Tiered Cache (one origin fetch per page per 5 min instead of one
per POP). Avoid a deploy between 19:00 and 24:00 on 29 Nov: it restarts the only Node process, discards the release's ISR
cache and purges the whole zone at peak (if `ELECTION_NIGHT_RESULTS_URL` must go in that night, do it as early as possible).
Capacity is one Node thread (~4–5 cold renders/s); a second process would need a shared cache handler (not for this week).

**How to re-measure.**
- Origin cache state and time through Cloudflare (a query string skips the HTML cache rule; Next ignores it):
  `curl -s -o /dev/null -D - -w 'ttfb %{time_starttransfer}\n' 'https://www.catalunyainfo.com/es/elecciones/suria/?pv=1' | grep -iE 'x-nextjs-cache|ttfb'`
  (MISS = a render, STALE = served + regenerated, HIT = cached). ≤ 1 req/s.
- The origin alone, on the VPS: the same `curl` on `http://127.0.0.1:3000/es/elecciones/<town>/` for towns not yet
  rendered since the last deploy.
- Prefetches per page view: load a town page in Chromium DevTools (Network, filter `_rsc`, phone size), scroll to the end:
  0 requests expected until a link is hovered or tapped (12 before this change).
- Cold start: after a deploy, the `warm` lines in the deploy log print each route's status and time.

**Outcome:** _pending — check on 30 Nov: origin load and slow requests on the night (Caddy access log: share of `_rsc`
requests and of responses > 3 s, compared with 18 Nov's 41 %)._

## 2026-11-24 — 29N pages after the night: past tense, "final result pending", "over" line, 8 Dec reset (body only; ca/es/en; groups `elections`)

**Why.** The 24 Nov election-night work left the pages true only up to the night: from Mon 30 Nov the callout still said "provisional results", the town slot and hub intro still promised "the same night" and "we will link the official site", and the hub still sent readers to the "how to vote" guides. No title, meta description, H1 or lead of any page is touched (the callout H2 and the 29N slot body are not among the four measured items).

**What changed.**
- `election-day.ts`, phase `after` (30 Nov to 7 Dec): provisional vs official in the past tense, the general count dated by the law (Fri 4 Dec, no later than Mon 7 Dec), proclamation and BOE publication within forty days, a "final official result: pending" line with the Interior election site and Infoelectoral (named as the election site and the data portal, not as results pages) while no results site is announced. The "checked on 24 Nov" date no longer prints after the night. Callout titles now say "official result pending the general count" (ca/es/en).
- `results-night.ts`: `resultsNightLine(locale, url, phase)`; `after` is past tense plus pending; `over` (from 8 Dec) says the vote was on 29 Nov, the night's figures were provisional, the count began 4 Dec and had to finish by 7 Dec, and links only the election site and Infoelectoral: no promise, no figure, no results link, no data import needed. Default phase is `before`, so the static guides (election night, Congress results) are unchanged.
- `model.ts` / `hub.ts` / the two page components pass the render-time phase; from 30 Nov the "if you have to vote" lines leave the town slot and the hub intro.
- 8 Dec reset: `revalidate` must be a static literal in this Next (16.3.5, caching guide: "needs to be statically analyzable"), so it cannot follow the clock. `scripts/election-layer-end.mjs` sets the eight routes back to `false`; `tests/election-day.test.ts` now FAILS from 8 Dec 00:00 Madrid (it failed only from 9 Dec) until the script is run and merged. Pages stop printing the layer by themselves at that instant.
- Law read on the BOE consolidated text (BOE-A-1985-11672, curl + grep, 24 Nov 2026; quotes in the `results-night.ts` comment): art. 103.1 "El escrutinio general se realiza el quinto día siguiente al de la votación", 107.2 "no más tarde del octavo día posterior al de las elecciones", 108.4 proclamation "dentro del día siguiente", 108.6 "en el periodo de cuarenta días, procederá a la publicación en el «Boletín Oficial del Estado»", 98.2 provisional information from the count-sheet copies. The ticket's "from the third day" is wrong: the text says the fifth (4 Dec), which is also the JEC calendar's 4-7 Dec.

**Baseline (GSC `snapshot.py families 7`, 24 Nov):** `/ca/eleccions/` and `/es/elecciones/` rows as printed that day (738 / 622 first column); run the same command for the review.

**Prediction.** No traffic effect expected: this keeps the pages true and fresh for readers searching "resultats eleccions 29N" on 30 Nov-7 Dec; judge only that the pages are not pulled for stale text.

**Review 2026-12-09:** `node scripts/election-layer-end.mjs` done and merged on 8 Dec (the guard test is red until then); the hub, a town and a comarca page show the `over` line; RESULTS_SITE_CHECKED and the guides (election night, Congress results) re-read: their static bodies still carry the pre-vote wording.

## 2026-11-24 — 29N guides correct from 30 Nov without an edit: `electionPhased` block (election-night, election-results, voting; ca/es/en; deploy, then groups `election-night election-results voting` BEFORE 30 Nov 00:05)

**Why.** After polling day the guides still spoke in the future: the election-night guide ("Interior has not announced its results site", "when Interior announces, we will add the link", the timetable in the present, the polls ban "is illegal"), the Congress-results guide (the 29N paragraph under the lead and "The next one: 29 November 2026"), and the how-to-vote guide ("the next election is the general election on 29 Nov", where to vote, hours and ID, hand in the postal vote by 26 Nov, the overseas vote, the FAQ). The hubs, comarca pages and town pages already switch by `electionPhase` (election-day.ts, `revalidate = 60`); these guides are DB-published articles with a stored body, so they could not.

**What changed (body only; no title, description, H1, heading of a kept section or lead moved, except the one clause below).**
- New block `electionPhased` (`blocks.ts`): `pre` (what the page always said), `after` (from Mon 30 Nov 00:00 Madrid), optional `over` (from Tue 8 Dec 00:00, else `after`). Variants are ordinary blocks stored as raw objects; `resolveElectionPhased(body, now)` (`content/election-phased.ts`) picks one with `electionPhase(now)`. The content page resolves it on the server before the table of contents and the FAQ JSON-LD are built (`[...slug]/page.tsx`), so the structured data follows the phase; the renderer also resolves it for any other caller; search text reads `pre`. The "count" phase (29 Nov from 20:00) reads `pre` on purpose: these pages re-render only at 00:05, so an evening variant would stay up all night.
- Revalidation: `electionPhased` joins `REVALIDATE_NIGHTLY_PATTERN` (`day-dependent.ts`), so the 00:05 cron re-renders the nine pages (30 Nov and 8 Dec are both covered; `after` starts 00:00, so at most five minutes of the old copy plus the CDN purge the cron already does). It is NOT in `DAY_DEPENDENT_BLOCKS`: the sitemap would have dated them "today" every night for the life of the page. Their `lastmod` is the phase start instead (`guidePhaseStart`, `contentLastModified` `phaseStart`, `SitemapRow.phased`): 30 Nov 00:00 Madrid, then 8 Dec 00:00; the election-day layer's earlier starts (28 Nov, 29 Nov 00:00 and 20:00) give none, since these pages read `pre` until 30 Nov.
- `election-after.ts`, `voting-after.ts`: the copy, ca/es/en, past tense. Facts all already in the guides, re-read on LOREG's consolidated text (BOE-A-1985-11672, 24 Nov): art. 98.2 (provisional information "que ha de proporcionar el Gobierno", from a copy of each table's count sheet), 103.1 ("el quinto día siguiente al de la votación", Fri 4 Dec), 107.2 ("no más tarde del octavo día posterior", Mon 7 Dec), 108.4 and 108.6 (proclamation; the JEC publishes in the BOE "en el periodo de cuarenta días"). The night's figures are written as the law's rule ("the law has the Government provide the provisional information"), not as observed; "within forty days" is art. 108.6's own wording ("en el periodo de cuarenta días", no anchor date), and the 8-16 Dec proclamation window (JEC calendar PDF, 403 to scripts on 24 Nov, last read 24 Oct) is left out of the `after`/`over` copy: art. 108.4's rule instead. **Observation (live crawl, 24 Nov 22:16 to 25 Nov 00:20 UTC, `npm run site:audit` with `SEO_UA=curl/8.5.0 SEO_MAX_RPS=3 SEO_CONCURRENCY=3`).**
Sitemap 3,319 URLs; 7,057 URLs crawled (every sitemap URL, then every internal page they link to: 3,737 more, all noindex), server
HTML, `<main>` links counted apart from the header (before `<main>`) and the footer (after it). Whole sitemap, no sampling.
Six URLs timed out once under the crawl (`/ca/eleccions/cabanes/`, `/ca/festius/celra/`, `/ca/festius/capellades/`,
`/es/festivos/das/`, `/es/festivos/sant-marti-vell/`, `/ca/festius/sant-marti-vell/`) and answered 200 on a re-fetch. **Not mine, for the
head: the three polls guides answer 500 live and are in the sitemap** (`/ca/guies/enquestes-eleccions-generals-catalunya/`,
`/es/guias/encuestas-elecciones-generales-cataluna/`, `/en/guides/spain-general-election-polls-catalonia/`; 25 Nov 00:20, "Internal Server Error").

| Inbound links per sitemap URL | 0 | 1-2 | 3-5 | 6-20 | >20 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Any link (menu and footer included) | **0** | 0 | 43 | 1,742 | 1,534 |
| In `<main>` (all linking pages, noindex ones too) | 3 | 25 | 121 | 1,752 | 1,418 |
| In `<main>`, from indexable pages only | 4 | 139 | 425 | 1,550 | 1,201 |

No orphan in the strict sense. The 3 pages with no body link are the legal hubs (`/ca|es|en/legal/`), reached from the footer of every page
(3,024 / 3,024 / 1,003 links) and left alone (footer untouched today). The honest count is the last row: Google gives little weight to links on pages
it does not index (`noindex, follow` ends up read as `nofollow`), and most town pages are noindex (low-demand.ts), so 143 indexable pages have two or fewer
body links from indexable pages (4,030 impressions in 28 days).

**Pages with at least 100 impressions in 28 days (GSC 28 Oct-24 Nov, `snapshot.py` helpers) and two or fewer body links.** All linking pages: 1
(`/en/christmas-markets/vic/`, 152 impr, 7 clicks, pos 6.4, 2 links). Indexable linking pages only: 8, with their impressions and links:
`/en/christmas-markets/vic/` 152 (2), `/en/holidays/2027/basque-country/bilbao/` 146 (2, pos 17.7), `/es/festivos/sant-marti-de-tous/` 127 (2),
`/ca/festius/porrera/` 123 (2), `/en/holidays/2027/murcia/mazarron/` 122 (1), `/es/elecciones/l-albiol/` 119 (1, 13 clicks, pos 4.3),
`/es/elecciones/sant-boi-de-llucanes/` 110 (2), `/ca/festius/2027/dia/29-marc/` 102 (1).
By family, the 143 pages (indexable sources, two or fewer): es elections 36, ca elections 29, ca holidays 24, es holidays 17, en holidays (2027 cities) 12,
legal 9, en elections 2, one each for 12 guides, events, price and about pages.

**Cause.** A town page links 12 neighbours "nearest in size in its comarca"; in a big comarca those are mostly noindex towns, so the few towns people search for
(Ordis, Sort, Porrera, l'Albiol) were linked from the hub and one neighbour. The 2027 city pages list their community's cities, all noindex in en/ca
except one or two (Mazarrón's 40 neighbours: none indexable). The English Christmas market pages (4 towns) picked their "nearby" towns from the 12 nearest
overall, none with an English page.

**Change (template level, ca/es/en as each family exists; every link names the town in the reader's language).**
- Holiday town pages ca/es (`MunicipalityPage`, `keptComarcaSiblings` in `holidays/data.ts`): the comarca list also names up to 6 indexable comarca-mates the
  neighbours list left out. Sibling-block links between indexable pages: towns with 2 or fewer, **ca 62 -> 30, es 59 -> 31** (of 341 / 306 indexable).
- Election town pages ca/es/en (`keptSiblings` in `elections/pages.ts`, used by `buildElectionPage`): same rule, up to 6; a page with fewer than 4 siblings in all
  (the English selection: Lleida, Girona) is topped up with the nearest indexable towns elsewhere in Catalonia. **ca 70 -> 6, es 73 -> 15, en 2 -> 2**.
- Spain 2027 city pages es/ca/en (`similarCities` in `spain-2027/cities.ts`): a city with fewer than 6 indexable neighbours in its community gets a
  "Cities of a similar size in other regions" list of indexable cities up to 6 (Mazarrón, Pamplona, Gandia). English indexable cities with 2 or fewer: **10 -> 3**; ca 3 -> 3
  (3 indexable cities in all); es: no inbound gain (outbound for single-city communities only).
- English Christmas market pages (`nearbyTowns(town, limit, accept)`, same-weekend limit): the English pages are chosen from every town. Girona and Figueres now link Vic (Vic: 2 links -> 4).
Rules kept: never a noindex target in the new links (`isLowDemandPath`), one link per target per page, no menu/footer/homepage change.

**Not done, with the reason.** Legal hubs (footer only; footer not touched today). `/ca/festius/2027/dia/29-marc/` (102 impr) and `/en/holidays/2027/day/8-september/`:

(1 body link, from the section hub: related cards live in the content database, a publish group). Electricity "tomorrow" pages (2 links; PVPC pages are off limits).
`/en/weekend/barcelona/` (1 link).

**Tests.** `tests/internal-link-weak-pages.test.ts` (new, 10): extra links only to indexable pages, same language, once, never self, not listed twice; weak-page counts
fall by a third (holidays), two thirds (elections) and a half (cities) against the sibling-only baseline, computed in the test so a change of the low-demand list at the
10 Dec review cannot fail it; Ordis linked from 3 or more indexable town pages; English padding; the components call the helpers; Christmas market `accept` runs before the limit.
Also green: election-municipal-pages, holiday-engine, holiday-english, christmas-fairs, christmas-markets, spain-cities-2027 (4 files), spain-holidays-2027-editions, spain-2027-council-towns,

## 2026-11-25 — Pay-dates guide: factual correction, "each unemployment payment is for the previous month" now sourced (ci-fonts + ci-edicio)

**URLs.** `/es/guias/cuando-se-cobra-paro-pension/`, `/ca/guies/quan-es-cobra-atur-pensio/`, `/en/guides/unemployment-benefit-pension-payment-dates-spain/` (group `pagos`).
Title, meta description, H1 and lead untouched (factual correction, allowed inside the 28-day window).

**Why.** A reviewer found no official source for the clause in the table column "Prestación que se cobra" and the SEPE paragraph (9 Nov). The SEPE FAQ does not say it. Found with curl on 25 Nov 2026:
BOE consolidated text of Real Decreto 625/1985 (ELI https://www.boe.es/eli/es/rd/1985/04/02/625/con, BOE-A-1985-8124, last update published 22/05/2024), art. 26.1:
«El abono de la prestación o subsidio por desempleo se realizará por mensualidades de treinta días, dentro del mes inmediato siguiente al que corresponda el devengo. En todo caso, el derecho al percibo de cada mensualidad caducará al año de su respectivo vencimiento.»
(The 24 Nov note "no 'mensualidades vencidas' wording" was right about the words, but the article says the same thing in other words.)

**Changed (ca/es/en).** The unsourced sentence is replaced by one citing RD 625/1985 art. 26.1 with the quote (es) or a close paraphrase (ca, en); the table note says the column follows art. 26.1 (thirty-day instalments, paid the following month); RD 625/1985 added to the sources. Pensions: no claim that they work the same; no source read for it (RD 696/2018 and the LGSS have no such sentence for ordinary pensions; LGSS «por meses vencidos» is only the delayed-retirement amount), so none is printed.
Test: `tests/pay-dates.test.ts` (+1). Not changed here: the unemployment calculator FAQ still omits the clause (its test forbids it); it could now cite art. 26.1.

**Baseline.** Unchanged from the 25 Nov entry of this guide (es 576 impressions / 10 clicks / pos 14.0; en 376 / 6 / 4.0; ca 59; 28 days to 24 Nov). A correction, not a ranking experiment; no prediction.
**Review** with the 2026-12-09 review of that entry. Re-read BOE art. 26.1 on or before 2027-01-25 (60 days).

- CCOO de Industria (state level), 19 Nov 2026 (`https://industria.ccoo.es/noticia:772972--El_27N_sera_un_viernes_negro_...`, HTTP 200; on its home page): «las personas que trabajan en el sector de la perfumería y la cosmética del Estado secundarán la primera de las tres jornadas de huelga que CCOO de Industria y UGT FICA han convocado»; «el sector volverá a parar el 23 de diciembre y el 4 de enero»; who is affected: «las trabajadoras que venden en sus tiendas artículos de perfumería y cosmética de las grandes marcas» (El Corte Inglés named) and «las plantillas de las fábricas que elaboran geles, champús y otros productos para supermercados como Mercadona».
- **Scope confirmed: Spain-wide** (the state-wide collective agreement; CCOO de Catalunya's 7,000 stays as «en el cas de Catalunya», attributed to CCOO de Catalunya). **Dates confirmed** by all three notices: 27 Nov, 23 Dec 2026, 4 Jan 2027. No hours in any notice.

## 2026-11-25 (night) — Christmas fairs pages answer like the Montserrat page: fact table and short FAQ on every town page and the hub; llms.txt names the top AI-landing pages and four family hubs it lacked (deploy; group `christmas`, llms.txt with the deploy; the fairs pages are programmatic)

**Why.** The AI-assistant analysis (GA4 channel "AI Assistant", 28 days to 25 Nov: 1,041 sessions, 2.8 % of the site) found the EN Montserrat page the model: the first sentence is the answer, 9 tables, FAQ. The EN Christmas markets Barcelona page got 29 AI sessions with 20 % engagement (users take the date from the assistant and leave) and the family had 0 tables and no FAQ on any page; Christmas markets are about 7 % of AI sessions (~70). The town leads already carry dates, place, "checked on <date>" and the official source (16 and 20 Nov entries), so they are not touched.

**Measurement windows respected.** Titles, descriptions, H1s and leads of the 49 town pages and the hubs are unchanged (the lead was changed on 16 and 20 Nov, inside 28 days; the hub lead and title were not touched either). Only new sections: a "Dades clau / Datos clave / Key facts" table, a FAQ, a hub table, and JSON-LD.

**What changed (template level, all towns, ca / es / en, data-driven; `lib/programmatic/christmas-fairs/facts.ts`, `page-facts.ts`, `components/.../facts-parts.tsx`):**
- **Fact table** after the "today" box on every town page, one small table per fair with only the rows its data has: Dates (with "organiser has not confirmed the 2026 edition" or "dates to be confirmed" next to them when the data says so), Hours (organiser's text; Mataró's "no hours published" is not shown as hours), Place, How to get there (the town's Rodalies/regional line and stations; lines only when the town has more than three, as Barcelona; no second train line when the organiser's own directions already name it; a pointer to the organiser's directions below when `details.access` exists), Tickets and prices (only `details.tickets`). Under it: source and reading date of each fair (organiser's page, calendar or agenda).
- **FAQ** (visible `dl`, and FAQPage JSON-LD built from the same items, `faqNode`): "When is the X fair 2026?" always; "What time does it open?", "Where is it?", "How to get there?", "Which tickets and prices?" only when the data answers; no FAQ when fewer than two can be answered. Each answer names where and when it was read. Multi-fair towns (Barcelona, Granollers, Tarragona) answer per fair.
- **Hub** (ca/es/en): table "Les principals fires de Nadal, d'un cop d'ull" with the fairs of the most searched towns (Barcelona, Girona, Vic, Tarragona, Olot, Canyelles, Espinelves, Caldes de Montbui, Cardedeu; in English only the towns with an English page), and a FAQ: how many fairs, which opens first and which closes last, and one question each for Barcelona, Girona, Vic and Tarragona (same strings as their pages, dates and hours), with FAQPage JSON-LD.
- `globals.css`: `.ci-facts` (label column + value, no stacking at 390 px).
- **llms.txt** (`lib/seo/llms.ts`, `topLandingTools`): Christmas markets in Barcelona (ca/es/en pages; was missing in English, 29 AI sessions), the four weekend zone pages with most AI visits (provincia-de-barcelona, barcelona, girona, costa-brava; 39 sessions), the official polls page (13) and the two family hubs that had no line at all: low-emission zones (ZBE) and blue-zone parking. Left out on purpose: `huelga-general-11-noviembre-sevilla` and `-madrid` (17 AI sessions): noindex since the strike (low-demand rule `strike-11n-cities`), and llms.txt never names a noindex URL.

**Baseline (GSC, 28 days to 25 Nov, `snapshot.py page`):** `/ca/fires-de-nadal/` 334 clicks / 11,919 impressions / position 6.5; `/es/mercados-navidad/` 399 / 17,506 / 7.3; `/en/christmas-markets/` 27 / 761 / 9.7 (of which `/en/christmas-markets/barcelona/` 1 / 217 / 16.5). AI assistant sessions (GA4, 28 days): EN christmas-markets/barcelona 29 (engagement 20 %), Christmas markets ~7 % of 1,041; Perplexity mercats-de-nadal a few. Weekend zone pages es 39, polls 13. No AI baseline for the other town pages (below the top-page list).

**Hypothesis.** A table and a FAQ with the date, hours, place and source in extractable form raise the chance that an assistant quotes the page with our URL and the reading date, and keep the AI visitor longer on the page (engagement above 20 %); organic: the "horari / com arribar / on es fa" sub-queries (Canyelles and Espinelves, 1-21 impressions each) now have a labelled answer. FAQPage on Google no longer yields a rich result for most sites, so no CTR effect is expected from it alone. llms.txt: no vendor documents using it for retrieval; cheap, effect not expected to be measurable.

**Review:** two reads, because most fairs end between 8 and 23 Dec. 2026-12-09: `snapshot.py page /fires-de-nadal/ 14`, `page /mercados-navidad/ 14`, `page /christmas-markets/ 14` against the baseline's daily rate (clicks per day: ca 11.9, es 14.2, en 1.0); GA4 AI Assistant landings on the three families (expect more than 29 on EN Barcelona in a 14-day window only if the assistants cite it again; engagement above 20 %); 2026-12-23 (full 28 days): the same plus the weekend zone and polls pages' AI sessions. ## 2026-11-25 - English editions of Christmas-market towns and weekend zones: evidence, decision NOT to open more (ci-demanda + ci-enginyeria)

**Question.** `scratchpad/night/ai-traffic.md`: ChatGPT sends 29 % of its sessions (304 of 1,041) to English pages, and only 6 towns (EN_TOWNS: Barcelona, Girona, Tarragona, Sitges, Vic, Figueres; Sitges has no dated fair, so no page) and 2 weekend pages (hub, Barcelona) exist in English. Which further English editions have demonstrated English demand?

**Threshold.** Open an English edition only if, on the ca/es/en pages of that town or zone in 28 days, at least one holds: >= 50 impressions of English-language queries (GSC), or >= 10 AI-assistant sessions with English browser language (GA4), or >= 10 sessions of any channel with English browser language landing on the ca/es pages. Reproducible: `$PY -I scripts/en-edition-demand.py 28` (new, read-only). Query language is a word-list heuristic; GSC hides rare queries, so impressions are a lower bound.

**Evidence (GSC 27 Oct-23 Nov, GA4 28 Oct-24 Nov; /en/ = impressions of the existing English page).**
| Candidate | EN-query impr | /en/ page impr | AI sessions (ca/es/en) | AI, English browser | English browser on ca/es pages | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Barcelona (market) | 86 | 103 | 29 | 7 | 0 | already open |
| Vic | 35 | 37 | 0 | 0 | 0 | already open; best of the rest ("vic christmas market" 28 impr, pos 7.6) |
| Girona (market) | 10 | 17 | 3 | 0 | 2 | already open; below threshold |
| Figueres (market) | 4 | 5 | 0 | 0 | 0 | already open; below |
| Tarragona (market) | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | already open (2 fairs); no demand seen |
| Sitges, Terrassa, Reus, Lleida (market) | 0 | - | 0 | 0 | 0-4 | cannot open: no dated fair in the snapshot (Sitges /en/ returns 404) |
| Sabadell, Granollers, Olot, Mataro, Badalona, Manresa (market) | 0 | - | 0-1 | 0 | 0-1 | rejected: zero English queries, zero English sessions |
| Weekend Barcelona | 5 | 5 | 12 | 2 | 2 | already open; 5 impr in 90 d |
| Weekend Girona | 0 | - | 9 | 1 | 1 | rejected |
| Weekend Costa Brava | 0 | - | 8 | 2 | 2 | rejected |
| Weekend Costa Daurada / Tarragona | 0 | - | 2 / 2 | 2 / 0 | 2 / 0 | rejected (2 sessions) |
| Weekend Pirineu | 0 | - | 1 | 0 | 0 | rejected |
| Weekend Sitges/Garraf, Montserrat area | - | - | - | - | - | no such zone (zones are Idescat/INE units; Sitges and Montserrat are day-trip guides, already in English) |
Context: all English pages together: 136k impressions in 90 d, but only 173 impressions for "christmas market" queries in 90 d site-wide, 120 of them on Barcelona/hub/Vic/Girona pages; ca/es fair and weekend pages got 0 English-query impressions in 90 d. English-language sessions on the ca/es fair+weekend pages: 43 in 28 d out of 692 (6 %), spread over 30 pages (max 2 per page).

**Decision.** No new English page. Nothing outside Barcelona reaches the threshold; the English AI traffic on Girona/Sitges/Tarragona/Montserrat (18 / 6 / 5 / 26 in 28 d) lands on the English day-trip guides, which already exist. The AI traffic to the weekend zone pages is Spanish-browser (67 of 77). The ai-traffic note's guess (+50-100 AI sessions/month from translating) is not supported by the numbers; a page opened without demand is a thin page. EN_TOWNS and ENGLISH_ZONES unchanged; nothing to publish, no sitemap/hreflang/llms.txt change.

**Not decided here (head).** Tarragona (0 impressions in 28 d) and Figueres (5) already have English pages without demand; they are not a noindex candidate yet (the season only started: Barcelona's English impressions went 0 to 93 per week in week 47, Girona 0 to 14), re-judge on the review date. Possible cheap link: the English Girona day-trip guide (18 AI sessions) links only the English market hub, not `/en/christmas-markets/girona/`.

**Review.** 2026-12-23: re-run `scripts/en-edition-demand.py 28` (window then covers the peak of the season, 25 Nov-22 Dec). Open an English edition for any town that passes; remove nothing before then. Candidates to watch: Girona (10 now), Vic (35), Figueres, weekend Costa Brava.

**Outcome:** _pending (2026-12-23)_
## 2026-11-25 (night) — Structured-data audit of the 50 most-shown pages and one page per template family: one Organization per page, one FAQPage per page, FAQ text = visible text (code only; no visible text, title, meta, H1 or lead changed)

**What was audited.** Live HTML of www.catalunyainfo.com (25 Nov, "curl/8.5.0", 2 req/s), 73 pages: the 50 pages with most impressions in the 28 days to 25 Nov (`snapshot.py pages 28 50`) plus Spain 2027 city (Sagunto), holiday towns (Sabadell, Terrassa) and day, election hub / comarca / town, Christmas-fair towns (Vic, Tremp, Valls), weekend hub and zones, three calculators, strike day (26N), Rodalies R3 / R11, fuel hub and province, reservoirs (Susqueda, Sau), 2027 bridges. Every `ld+json` script parsed; rules: invalid JSON, more than one FAQPage, FAQ question and answer text found in the visible text, Article dates (modified before published, in the future), Event required fields and ended events, BreadcrumbList names against the visible trail, empty Dataset / Place / Event fields, one `@id` with two different values. The same rules now live in `scripts/lib/page-checks.ts` (`npm run site:audit`), so the next crawl reports them site-wide.

**Before (live, 73 pages).** Invalid JSON-LD 0. Pages with more than one FAQPage 0. FAQ questions or answers not in the visible text 0. Article dates wrong 0. Event missing name / startDate / location 0. Breadcrumb names different from the visible trail 0. Empty Dataset / Place fields 0. **Conflicting `@id`: 47 pages** (every Article / NewsArticle page): the layout's Organization (`#organization`, `url` = `https://www.catalunyainfo.com/`, with alternateName, email, sameAs, founder) and the Article's inline `publisher` under the same `@id` (shorter, `url` without the slash). Article without `image`: 10 (the 11N city-strike guides, which have no photograph; left as is, a generic card would be a picture of something else). Event of a past fair still `EventScheduled`: 1 (Canyelles, ended 22 Nov; true to the schema, which also means "took place as scheduled"; reported as info only).
The FAQ blocks added on 24-25 Nov (fairs, strikes, weekend, money pages) are not all live yet; their code was checked instead: one FAQPage per template (`faqNode`, `weekendFaqNode`, `faqSchema(entry.body)`), and every Christmas-fair town and hub (ca/es/en) and every Spain 2027 hub and city (ca/es/en, over 1,500 pages) has distinct, non-empty questions and no markup left on screen.

**Fixed (template level).**
- `publisherNode` of the Article is now the layout's own `organizationSchema(locale)`: same `@id`, same properties, so the 47 contradictions go (also the author page's `worksFor`).
- `faqSchema` builds the answer with the page's own formatter (`lib/content/inline-text.ts`, split from `inline.tsx`; `renderInline` and the JSON-LD share one tokenizer) instead of a regex that also deleted every lone `*`, `_` and backtick the page shows, and keeps a link whose href the page does not turn into a link as text.
- `faqSchema(body)` merges all FAQ blocks of a body into one FAQPage (it kept only the first, so a second visible FAQ was missing from the markup); `graph()` merges any two FAQPage nodes into one, drops a second BreadcrumbList and a node repeated as is.
- Audit rules added: `jsonld-faq-multiple`, `jsonld-faq-answer-not-visible`, `jsonld-article-modified-in-future`, `jsonld-event-past` (info), `breadcrumb-names-differ`, `jsonld-empty-field`, `jsonld-id-conflict`.

**Tests.** New `tests/jsonld-rules.test.ts` (7: one FAQPage and one BreadcrumbList after `graph()`; several FAQ blocks become one FAQPage; answer text = what `renderInline` prints; Article publisher = layout Organization; FAQ items of every fairs town and hub and of every Spain 2027 hub and city, ca/es/en: no repeated question, no markup on screen, JSON-LD = items); `tests/site-audit-checks.test.ts` +7 (one test per audit rule). 19 existing test files that cover JSON-LD (structured-data, calculators-jsonld, christmas-*, weekend-facts, holiday-*, spain-*, strike-citable, seo, discover-news …) pass; `tsc --noEmit` clean. `seo:body-dates` not run (no visible content changed).

**After.** Expected on the live HTML after the deploy and the pages' revalidation: conflicting `@id` 0 of the same 73 pages (47 before); everything else unchanged at 0. Check with `npm run site:audit` (codes above) or the same fetch of the 73 pages.

**Review.** 2026-12-02 (after the deploy): re-fetch the 73 pages, expect `jsonld-id-conflict` 0 and no new `jsonld-faq-*`; run `npm run site:audit` and read the new codes site-wide (weekend and Christmas-fair FAQs once live). Search Console, Enhancements, 2026-12-09: no new Article / Event / Breadcrumb errors. No traffic effect expected (FAQ rich results ended in May; Article publisher is a trust signal, not a ranking one).
